about: Savory & James is a sherry label with a long American story. It belongs to Charles Jacquin et Cie of Philadelphia, a firm founded in 1884 by a French émigré that calls itself the oldest cordial producer in the United States, and it covers a small range of fortified wines: fino, amontillado and cream sherries, plus tawny and ruby port. The sherries are made and aged in Spain’s Jerez district, in the bodegas of Fernando A. de Terry, a historic house of El Puerto de Santa María.

Like all sherry, it begins with white grapes, chiefly Palomino, grown in the chalk-white albariza soils of the Jerez region. The young wine is fortified and aged in a solera, a tiered system of casks in which a little of the oldest wine is drawn off for bottling and topped up with younger wine from the row above, so each bottle is a blend of many years. Cream sherry is the sweet style, rounded with Pedro Ximénez; this solera is said to have been established in 1780.

Expect dried figs, raisins, toasted almonds and caramel on the nose, with toffee and roasted nuts on a full, velvety palate and a gently bittersweet, nutty finish. Serve it lightly chilled in a small glass at the end of the meal. It is also the traditional base for a Sherry Cobbler or a Sherry Flip.
